item.title: How do I stay informed about BioCurious events?
item.description: All our meetings, events, and projects are organized with Meetup. Sign up at meetup.com/biocurious to stay informed.

item.title: Can I do my own project or research in the lab?
item.description: Yes! You must first become a member, submit your project for safety committee review, and pass the safety test. BioCurious is a Biosafety Level 1 (BSL-1) lab.

item.title: Who comes to BioCurious?
item.description: People from many backgrounds — from those who last took biology in high school to professional scientists, artists, and social scientists. Anyone is welcome to join community projects for free. Lab work requires membership.

item.title: What is a Citizen Scientist?
item.description: A Citizen Scientist is an amateur or non-professional scientist participating in scientific research, creating open dialogue between professional research and the general public.

item.title: Can I visit?
item.description: Email info@biocurious.org and we can schedule a time to show you around. For events or community projects, join our Meetup Group.

item.title: How do I become a member?
item.description: Sign up online through our Membership page. We ask that members fill out a membership agreement and pay dues. After signing up, you must pass the safety test before entering the lab.

item.title: What about Youth Membership (Under 18)?
item.description: All members under 18 must enroll through a Family Membership. A parent or guardian must accompany and supervise minors at all times. Both must pass safety certification, and all projects require safety committee approval.

item.title: Isn't allowing people to work in a biology lab dangerous?
item.description: Our lab functions at Biosafety Level 1 (BSL-1), equivalent to a high school biology lab. All members undergo safety orientation and must pass a safety test before using the lab.

item.title: How do I become a volunteer?
item.description: If you are over 18 and interested in volunteering, contact info@biocurious.org with information about yourself and how you would like to help.

item.title: Donations
item.description:
We’ll make good use of consumables, gear, and reagents. Consider also donating to our friends at BioLink Depot.

Contact us at info@biocurious.org before sending anything.

✓ We want

  • FBS, HPLC columns, lab consumables
  • Working equipment and useful reagents

✗ We don’t want

  • Fluorescent bulbs, cadmium chloride, HPLC waste, hazardous materials

item.title: Events
item.description:
Join one of our Open Lab nights, a community project jam session, a lecture, or a technical class. All events are organized through Meetup.

We welcome newcomers — no experience necessary.

View Events on Meetup →

item.title: Projects
item.description:
We have had many projects in the past and are always organizing more.

🧬 CRISPR Class

Newbie friendly — Crash course on molecular biology and cloning. From zero to disrupting a gene in a month.

🧀 Real Vegan Cheese

Recruiting — What is the essence of cheese, and can we make it in a flask? An ongoing community bioengineering project.

🔧 Fix or Teardown?

Self-directed — We often have broken gear to fix or teardown into useful components. Like hardware? We need help.
